card st-build-died-cap  [open]
A fresh pass after a death uses the retry cap that the dead build ran with
why: A build started with a custom cap must stop at that cap. A fixed default in the server would let it run too long or stop too early.

The start of a build records its retry cap in the board log. The server reads that cap when it restarts a dead build, and passes it to the fresh pass. A start with no recorded cap, from an earlier version, uses the default cap of the build.

  -> refines         st-build-died  The server restarts a build whose process died, as a fresh pass
card st-build-died-detached  [open]
A restarted build runs in its own process group and outlives the server
why: A build that the server restarts must survive a stop of the server, or an interrupt of the server would kill the fresh pass and count as one more death against the cap.

The server starts the fresh pass through the public command line of the build, as a separate process in its own process group, and does not wait for it. The build takes a flag that names the dead session. The fresh pass continues the dead build: it keeps the build identity and the card obligation that the first pass opened, and opens no new obligation. The server still learns of the exit, to look for dead builds again.

  -> refines         st-build-died  The server restarts a build whose process died, as a fresh pass
card st-build-died-record  [open]
A death is recorded as a red pass with no cost
why: The board and the measures read passes and steps. A death must show there as a failed pass, so the count of passes and the failure reasons stay true.

The end written for a dead build carries died as its reason. The server also records the dead pass as a red pass on the ticket, and as an ended pass step in the pipeline log with died as the reason, zero wall time and no cost, because the dead process cannot report either.

  -> refines         st-build-died  The server restarts a build whose process died, as a fresh pass

card st-build-died  [decided]
The server restarts a build whose process died, as a fresh pass
why: A build runs in its own process, apart from the server, so a server restart does not stop it. But the build process itself can die: a kill, a crash, a machine sleep. Nothing inside that process can see its own death, so the server, which already checks whether each build process is alive, writes the end and starts a fresh pass from the work already committed on the ticket's branch.
subtree: 4 cards, 3 open, 1 decided

**The problem.** A ticket whose build process died sits in building with no pulse (#vi-board-session-file). Nobody starts it again, so the run stops until a person sees it.

**The answer.** The server is the watcher. It looks for a dead build at two moments: when a build process it started exits, and when the server itself starts. A build counts as dead when the board log has a start for it, no end, and its process is gone. For each one the server does three things. It writes the end, with died as the reason. It starts a fresh pass of the same ticket, from the last commit on the ticket's branch, with the death as the last failure in the brief (#lp-stateless). The fresh pass counts against the ticket's retry cap, so a build that dies on every pass still stops (#st-build-silence-act treats a silent pass the same way).

A pass does not resume the agent's own conversation. Work the dead pass did not commit is lost: at most one pass of work. The session id stays in the session log for a person who wants to read what the dead pass did.

While the server is down, nothing watches. A build keeps running without the server; a build that dies in that time is found when the server starts again.

**Example.**

- Ticket T "r/03" sits in building. Its branch has two commits from earlier passes.
- Pass 3 runs in process P. It has edited files and not committed them.

1. A person closes the laptop lid. P dies. The server is down too.
2. The person starts werk. The server reads the board log: pass 3 of T started, has no end, and P is dead.
3. The server writes the end of pass 3: died. The edits that pass 3 did not commit are gone.
4. The server starts pass 4 of T from the second commit. The brief says that pass 3 died.
5. Pass 4 is the last pass the retry cap allows. If it dies too, T stops with died as the reason, and the server starts nothing more.
6. A build whose process is alive is left alone, whether this server started it or an earlier one did.

# Every task a person or an agent runs on werk is a target here.
# A target's description is the text after "##" on its line.

PINNED_BUN := $(shell cat .bun-version)
STAMP := node_modules/.install-stamp

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help
.PHONY: help bun-version install lint lint-fix typecheck test test-coverage e2e check dev smoke release-build

help: bun-version ## List every target with its description
	@grep -E '^[a-z0-9-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | \
		sed -E 's/^([a-z0-9-]+):.*## (.*)$$/\1\t\2/' | \
		awk -F'\t' '{ printf "  %-14s %s\n", $$1, $$2 }'

bun-version:
	@installed="$$(bun --version 2>/dev/null)"; \
	if [ "$$installed" != "$(PINNED_BUN)" ]; then \
		echo "werk: wrong Bun version." >&2; \
		echo "werk: installed: $${installed:-none}" >&2; \
		echo "werk: pinned:    $(PINNED_BUN) (file .bun-version)" >&2; \
		echo "werk: install it with: curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash -s \"bun-v$(PINNED_BUN)\"" >&2; \
		exit 1; \
	fi

# Installs the locked packages when the package file or the lock file changed.

card vi-board-session-file  [decided]
A builder session runs only while the board log says it started and its process is still alive
why: A builder runs in its own process and can die without a word, for example when a person kills it by hand. A flag in a log alone then says it still runs, and the ticket pulses forever. So the board also checks the process itself, and keeps the agent's many lines out of the board log so that log stays a short record of ticket state.


card st-build-silence-act  [decided]
On silence, the overseer cancels the session and a fresh pass starts
why: A stall from a rate limit or a retry storm goes away on a new session. One silent pass is no evidence that the ticket cannot be built.


card st-grade-defer  [decided]
On the last counted pass, small gaps in built cards merge and become a follow-up ticket
why: A ticket whose only remaining problems are small gaps in cards it did build would otherwise reach the retry cap and park, with all its work unmerged and every ticket after it waiting. Merging it and filing the gaps as a ticket of their own keeps the work moving and keeps each gap visible on the board.


card lp-stateless  [decided]
The loop is stateless per pass
why: Long contexts degrade. The file system and git do not.

The three `st-build-died-*` cards (#st-build-died-cap, #st-build-died-detached, #st-build-died-record) are decided. The code in werk-v0 matches all three by reading, but I did not run its tests.

I read werk-v0, the build target. I did not read the prototype in this worktree.

- **Cap:** `build.started` records the cap. The fold reads it back, and the server passes `--cap` to the fresh pass. A start with no cap uses the default of 5.
- **Detached:** the server starts the build detached, in its own process group, with `--after-death <session>`. The fresh pass reuses the build id. It opens no second obligation, and it releases the dead pass's branch.
- **Record:** the server writes `build.ended` with `died`, a red `ticket.pass`, and a `step.ended` with zero time and no cost.

Tests: the died and dead-builds test files exist for all three behaviours. They fail to start because `node_modules` is missing in werk-v0, so no test ran.

On the map, each card now has two `depends_on` edges, to #st-build-ticket and #vi-board-session-file. A card cannot depend on its own parent, #st-build-died. Each card also has one manual kill criterion with a review date of 2027-01-26. I wrote the criteria myself. Please check that they say what would change your mind.
